question.text: Neha invested INR 5,00,000 which grew to INR 8,05,255 over 5 years. What is the CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate)?

explanation.text: The Logic: CAGR = (Terminal Value / Initial Value)^(1/n) - 1 = (8,05,255 / 5,00,000)^(1/5) - 1 = (1.61051)^0.2 - 1 = 1.10 - 1 = 10.00%. Verification: 5,00,000 × (1.10)^5 = 5,00,000 × 1.61051 = 8,05,255. The Trap: 12.20% uses simple return divided by years [(8,05,255 - 5,00,000)/5,00,000]/5 = 12.21%, which is the simple annualized return, not CAGR. 9.50% and 11.00% result from arithmetic errors in the nth root calculation.
